original_formulation: Aggressive PTQ selectively increases an AI agent's reliance on misleading observational associations (Delta(p) = ConflictPenalty(p) - ConflictPenalty(F16) > 0) beyond general task degradation.
motivation: Motivating course-project hypothesis linking LLM compression to vulnerability to confounding shortcuts.
supporting_evidence: None isolating causal-specific vulnerability from response bias, format invalidity, or control-task failures.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: In 005 and 011, Q4_K_M reduced the measured conflict penalty (-43.75 pp and -39.06 pp) due to near-constant activation; in 024, Qwen F16 vs Q4_K_M semantic causal accuracy differed by -0.4 pp while F16 references failed harmful-direction controls.
alternative_explanations: Constant action bias, Markdown/length-cap invalidity, prompt-order sensitivity, and general arithmetic/control weakness.

original_formulation: A homogeneous 3-parameter CNI-style multinomial processing tree P(activate|T,S) = C*T + (1-C)[A*S + (1-A)*B] validly decomposes LLM intervention choices into causal sensitivity C, conditional association A, and action bias B.
motivation: Adapted from Jacoby (1991), Gawronski et al. (2017), and Wu & Deng (2025) to separate cue sensitivity from action tendency.
supporting_evidence: Synthetic EM parameter recovery succeeded in interior regimes; crossing T and S successfully exposed constant-action bias.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Synthetic validation proved symmetric logistic integration is observationally equivalent on 4 cells; Cohort 005 F16 violated the tree's required additivity equality p11 - p10 - p01 + p00 = 0 by -43.75 pp (CI [-68.75, -18.75]).
alternative_explanations: Presentation-order interactions, symmetric cue integration, and direction-asymmetric policies.

original_formulation: Qwen2.5-3B Q2_K increases the aligned-minus-conflict accuracy gap relative to 3B F16 on exact-evidence direct-response SCM tables.
motivation: First empirical pilot test of H01 using extreme 2-bit GGUF quantization.
supporting_evidence: None (post hoc +3.125 pp contrast was an artifact of 0/64 Q2_K floor vs 16/32 and 17/32 F16).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Q2_K produced 0/64 valid responses (all 64 length-capped repetitive punctuation); 3B F16 itself activated on 63/64 items and got 0/64 adjustment sets.
alternative_explanations: Catastrophic low-bit generation instability at Q2_K and baseline incompetence at 3B F16.

original_formulation: The 3B Q2_K output collapse is caused by llama.cpp's default CPU weight repacking or mismatched GGUF tokenizer/chat-template metadata.
motivation: Software/runtime diagnostic before attributing Q2_K failure to quantized weights.
supporting_evidence: None.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Disabling CPU repacking (--no-repack) changed token strings on 16/16 tasks but still yielded 0/16 valid outputs and 16/16 length caps; GGUF tokenizer and chat templates matched across F16, Q4_K_M, and Q2_K with identical prompt token counts on 64/64 tasks.
alternative_explanations: Intrinsic Q2_K weight quantization degradation on Qwen2.5-3B without importance-matrix calibration.

original_formulation: Explicitly supplying the backdoor adjustment formula improves explicit binary decision accuracy on exact SCM tables.
motivation: Test whether Cohort 001 failures stemmed from inability to identify the causal adjustment formula rather than arithmetic execution.
supporting_evidence: Improved numeric ATE estimate accuracy (MAE fell from 0.246 to 0.062 in F16) and estimate-sign accuracy (34/64 to 61/64 in F16).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Explicit binary action accuracy did NOT improve: F16 scored 32/64 (0/64 activate, flipping from 63/64 activate to 64/64 decline) and Q4_K_M scored 35/64 (3/64 activate), frequently contradicting the model's own numeric sign.
alternative_explanations: Dissociation between numeric computation field and binary action commitment; prompt framing shifted default action bias.

original_formulation: Under the supplied arithmetic formula, Q4_K_M degrades the sign accuracy of computed numeric estimates relative to F16 and Q8_0 on Qwen2.5-3B.
motivation: Observed 61/64 vs 45/64 sign gap in Cohort 002; tested against Q8_0 (006) and replicated on 12 fresh families (007).
supporting_evidence: Cohort 006 Q8_0 tied F16 at 61/64 (+25.0 pp over Q4_K_M); Cohort 007 fresh families replicated F16 46/48 vs Q4_K_M 31/48 (-31.25 pp, 95% CI [-41.67, -20.83]).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Degradation occurred across both aligned and conflict cells, so it reflects numerical execution rather than causal conflict susceptibility.
alternative_explanations: Arithmetic rounding/calculation errors under 4-bit weight compression in a 3B model.

original_formulation: Scaling full-precision reference size from 3B to 7B (Qwen2.5-7B F16) establishes above-gate causal conflict competence on unscaffolded direct or minimal supplied-rate prompts.
motivation: Larger model capacity expected to resolve 3B reference floor before quantization testing.
supporting_evidence: 7B F16 correctly named adjustment set [Z] on 32/32 items in Cohort 004 and solved 32/32 aligned items in Cohorts 012-014.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Failed predeclared gates in Cohort 004 (17/32 overall, 31/32 activate), Cohort 012 (8/16 & 7/16 conflict), Cohort 013 minimal (8/16 conflict), and Cohort 014 minimal (8/16 conflict).
alternative_explanations: Persistent activation bias on conflict items when confounding mechanism is left implicit.

original_formulation: Physical presentation order of randomized versus historical evidence shifts Qwen2.5-3B F16 conflict decisions toward lower accuracy when historical evidence appears first.
motivation: Motivated by family-level order split in Cohort 005; tested via cross-session reversal (008), same-session interleaving (009), fresh families (010), and matched signal strength (011).
supporting_evidence: Consistently replicated in 3B F16: -28.125 pp (008), -21.875 pp (009), -25.0 pp on fresh families (010), and -25.0 pp under matched observational strength (011).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Aligned accuracy shifted in the opposite direction (+29.2 to +43.75 pp), showing directional/positional response shifts rather than pure historical-distractor capture.
alternative_explanations: Line-position sensitivity interacting with baseline activation tendency.

original_formulation: Equalizing observational signal magnitude |delta_obs| across aligned and conflict cells eliminates the aligned-versus-conflict difficulty confound and yields competent reference conflict decisions.
motivation: Mathematical audit showed original generator had |delta_obs| = confounding + |tau| in aligned vs confounding - |tau| in conflict.
supporting_evidence: Mathematical validators confirmed exact interior probabilities and matched historical gaps m in [0.38, 0.46).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Did not yield conflict competence: 3B F16 conflict stayed 24/64 (011) and 7B F16 conflict stayed 15/32 (012). Later retrospective audit of 016 revealed that because |tau| < m everywhere, a source-blind smaller-gap heuristic could solve 100% of items.
alternative_explanations: Model conflict errors were not caused solely by larger aligned gaps, and fixed |tau| < m created a magnitude-separation shortcut.

original_formulation: Adding explicit causal-context explanations with a strict one-key bare-JSON response contract (48-token cap) restores response validity and enables 7B F16 to pass reference qualification.
motivation: Cohort 013 causal-context prose triggered 64/64 trailing explanations hitting the 160-token cap.
supporting_evidence: Strict JSON validity rose from 0/64 (013) to 64/64 (014) and 128/128 (015); Cohort 015 F16 narrowly passed all gates (89/128 overall vs 88, conflict 19/32 & 22/32 vs 18).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Cohort 014 missed overall threshold by 2 (42/64 vs 44), and Cohort 016 F16 conflict accuracy dropped back to 76/192 (39.6%) and 109/192 (56.8%) on 96 fresh families, showing Cohort 015's marginal gate pass was fragile.
alternative_explanations: Sampling variability on 16 families and strong presentation-order dependence.

original_formulation: On the strict-JSON causal-context source-selection task, Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M exhibits a nonzero within-family conflict accuracy difference between historical-first and randomized-first presentation.
motivation: Prospectively frozen confirmatory replication on 96 fresh families (powered for >=20 pp at 80.7% power) after observing +65.6 pp in Cohort 015.
supporting_evidence: Prospectively confirmed on 96 untouched families: 175/192 (91.1%) historical-first vs 55/192 (28.6%) randomized-first, mean difference +62.5 pp (95% t CI [+56.6, +68.4], t(95)=21.10, p=1.24e-37).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Aligned items moved oppositely (192/192 rand-first to 105/192 hist-first), and retrospective audit showed a source-blind smaller-gap heuristic solves 768/768 prompts, so high historical-first conflict accuracy does not prove causal provenance use.
alternative_explanations: Position-linked action/recency heuristics rather than principled backdoor reasoning.

original_formulation: The large positive conflict-order effect (+62.5 pp) observed in Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M generalizes to Qwen2.5-14B quantized checkpoints (Q8_0 and Q4_K_M) on the same 96-family schedule.
motivation: Exploratory cross-scale test of whether the Cohort 016 order phenomenon is a general property of quantized Qwen2.5 models.
supporting_evidence: None on conflict items (though aligned items still dropped from 192/192 and 152/192 rand-first to 96/192 hist-first).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: 14B Q8_0 conflict order effect was -4.17 pp (95% CI [-6.98, -1.35]) and 14B Q4_K_M was exactly 0.0 pp (96/192 in both orders due to 100% activation on conflict items).
alternative_explanations: Checkpoint-scale differences in default activation bias mask or alter conflict-cell order effects.

original_formulation: Intervention decision accuracy increases monotonically with causal effect magnitude (0.12 vs 0.04) and remains invariant to neutral output-token remapping.
motivation: Signal-detection and psychometric construct-validity requirements from Interdisciplinary Follow-Up.
supporting_evidence: Isolated mapping comprehension checks passed 16/16 (018) and 48/48 (019).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: In Cohort 018, F16 scored 32/64 at both 0.04 and 0.12 strengths (d'=0 at 0.12); in Cohort 019, semantic accuracy was 37/64 (0.04) vs 36/64 (0.12), while reversing neutral tokens K/M shifted accuracy by +25.8 pp causal and +36.7 pp noncausal on identical stems.
alternative_explanations: Token-label preference and multi-step working-memory interference when remapping actions.

original_formulation: Qwen2.5-7B F16 fails two-source causal decisions because it cannot identify which study is randomized or which study should govern an intervention decision.
motivation: Component decomposition diagnostic separating rate reading, source identification, governing-study selection, and two-source action choice.
supporting_evidence: None for source-identification deficit; strong evidence for component-vs-integration dissociation.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Qwen 7B F16 achieved 32/32 direct source identification (020, 021, 022), 128/128 governing-study selection (021, 022), 244/256 (023), 242/256 (024), and 90.6%-100% randomized-only decision accuracy, while two-source decisions scored 43.3%-45.3%. Explicit source guidance in 021 gave 58/128 vs 58/128 ordinary.
alternative_explanations: Two-source contextual interference and activation bias during joint rate-to-action mapping (note: separate fresh-context prompts do not prove internal sequential mediation).

original_formulation: Qwen2.5-7B F16's two-source causal decision deficit (+53 to +57 pp below randomized-only) generalizes cleanly across independent model families (Mistral-7B-v0.3, Llama-3.1-8B) and is specific to causal tasks relative to matched harmful-direction controls.
motivation: Cross-lineage replication (022, 024) and within-Qwen discriminant control audit (023, 024).
supporting_evidence: Within Qwen 7B F16, the +53.1 pp (022), +55.5 pp (023), and +56.6 pp (024) randomized-only minus two-source gap repeated reliably across fresh seeds, A/B names, and option orders.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Mistral failed simple components (selected first displayed option on 256/256 source prompts in 024); Qwen and Llama failed harmful-direction numeric (18/32) and noncausal scorecard (75/128, 71/128) robustness thresholds (<75%).
alternative_explanations: Directional bias against declining/harmful actions affects both causal and noncausal rate tasks; Mistral uses positional heuristics.

original_formulation: Across a 3-lineage (Qwen 7B, Mistral 7B, Llama 8B) x 7-format (F16 to Q2_K) GGUF matrix, post-training quantization produces a monotone degradation in causal decision accuracy or a selective causal-minus-control penalty.
motivation: Comprehensive multi-lineage quantization screen on 1,472 identical tasks per arm (30,912 attempts).
supporting_evidence: Extreme Q2_K degraded output validity in Mistral (129 invalids) and increased first-option bias in Qwen source selection (96.9%).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Semantic causal accuracy was flat from F16 to Q4_K_M in Qwen (111 vs 110/256), Mistral (134 vs 130/256), and Llama (151 vs 150/256), rose in Qwen Q3/Q2 (150, 149/256) due to policy shifts, and Llama Q4_K_M suffered 448/1472 length-capped invalids almost exclusively in noncausal controls (0/256 strict semantic control) while recovering to 225/256 at Q3_K_M.
alternative_explanations: Non-monotone quantizer/format interactions with generation length and response policy.

original_formulation: F16 reference models (Qwen 3B/7B, Mistral 7B, Llama 8B) can adapt unaided intervention choices to observationally identical confounder versus mediator causal graphs across both answer-option orders.
motivation: Graph-switch assay holding P(W,X,Y) exact-rational identical while reversing sign(E[Y|do(X=1)]-E[Y|do(X=0)]).
supporting_evidence: Llama 8B F16 read upstream/downstream graph structure at 31/32 on Cohort 027 direct form.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Cohort 026's apparent 6/8 Llama decision switch score was confounded with option position (61/64 first-option choices) and failed W->Z no-change controls (0/8 on W->Z). In order-balanced Cohort 027, order-robust paired switch fidelity was 0/8 families across ALL four F16 models and BOTH forms, and matched arithmetic was 15/32-17/32.
alternative_explanations: Failure on both weighted arithmetic execution and graph-to-procedure mapping, plus severe option-order sensitivity.

original_formulation: Offloading arithmetic execution to an exact deterministic calculator (System C) enables F16 models (Qwen 7B, Llama 8B) to qualify on causal graph-switch decisions by selecting the correct graph-conditioned weighting procedure ('marginal' vs 'conditional').
motivation: Cohort 027 arithmetic failures left open whether models understood graph identification rules but failed arithmetic.
supporting_evidence: Deterministic calculator C dramatically improved matched noncausal named-rule tasks (Qwen 58/128 -> 128/128; Llama 68/128 -> 112/128), proving arithmetic execution was a major bottleneck on controls.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: On causal graph-switch tasks, C-minus-B gain was +2.34 pp for Qwen (CI [-3.91, +9.38]) and -8.59 pp for Llama (CI [-13.28, -3.91]); specificity was -52.34 pp and -42.97 pp. Causal rule selection hovered near chance (~50%) even when candidate scores were pre-computed.
alternative_explanations: Models failed to map confounder vs mediator DAG descriptions onto marginal vs conditional weighting rules when unassisted by explicit graph-to-formula instructions.

original_formulation: On CF-TP1's independent transfer form, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M exhibits different paired target-population fidelity on causal provenance-and-transport decisions than on matched explicit-scorecard weighted arithmetic (Delta != 0).
motivation: Final prospective 128-family, 4,096-call frozen case study breaking Cohort 016's magnitude shortcut and pairing feasible provenance swaps with target-mixture switches.
supporting_evidence: Point estimate was in the expected negative direction: causal 128/512 (25.00%) vs arithmetic 146/512 (28.52%), Delta = -3.515625 pp.
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: The prespecified approximate 95% Welch-Satterthwaite t interval [-7.7713, +0.7400] pp and bounded interval [-27.5237, +20.4924] pp both cross zero; archive-compatible form yielded 128/512 in both tasks (Delta = 0.0 pp). No equivalence margin was prespecified.
alternative_explanations: Both tasks suffered low end-to-end paired fidelity under different error regimes: near-constant activation on causal prompts (995/1024, 3/256 reversals) versus frequent uncalibrated switching on arithmetic prompts (46/256 required switches, 45/256 unwarranted invariant flips).

original_formulation: Multi-step interactive tool-using causal agents or layer-wise mixed-precision restoration isolate behavioral or mechanistic quantization effects on causal discovery and estimation.
motivation: Original Roadmap Phase 5 and Literature Review proposals (CausaLab, ACDB, PRISM, Zhang et al. 2025).
supporting_evidence: None (Cohort 028 implemented a one-shot offline replay calculator, not an interactive multi-turn agent or neural weight-patching intervention).
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: Not contradicted; deliberately deferred after direct-response construct-validity gates repeatedly stopped advancement.
alternative_explanations: N/A (unexecuted prospective extension).
